jobs.occupation: DGI Storkøbenhavn søger idrætskonsulent til gymnastik (barselsvikariat)
jobs.description:
Vil du være en del af en organisation, som går forrest i udviklingen af idrætsforeninger?

Har du en faglighed inden for gymnastik og et stærkt foreningskendskab? 

Brænder du for at sammensætte og drive de helt rigtige kurser og uddannelser?

Så er du måske vores nye kollega i DGI Storkøbenhavn.

Vi søger en konsulent, som kan arbejde strategisk og er en drivkraft i udviklingen af gymnastikken i Storkøbenhavn. Med udgangspunkt i din faglige viden og erfaring skal du samarbejde med gymnastikforeningerne om udvikling, aktiviteter og uddannelse af instruktører og ledere.

Du understøtter gymnastikforeningerne i deres dagligdag og er deres sparringspartner og rådgiver. Du skal derfor kunne skabe gode relationer til nøglepersoner i gymnastikforeningerne samtidig med, at du kan inddrage kolleger med forskellige andre fagligheder. 

Det er især vigtigt, at du kan drive og udvikle vores kursus- og uddannelsesområde, så vores tilbud til gymnastikforeninger, frivillige og instruktører er attraktive og af høj kvalitet. 
Dine opgaver bliver blandt andet at

• løbende kvalificere vores udbud af kurser og uddannelser
• afdække behov hos foreninger og omsætte dem til relevante tilbud
• udvikle nye kurser, uddannelser og skræddersyede forløb
• rekruttere de rette undervisere og samarbejde tæt med dem
• arbejde med synlighed og øge deltagelsen på vores kurser
DGI Storkøbenhavn har desuden indgået en række kommunepartnerskaber med henblik på at skabe de bedste forudsætninger for foreningsidrætten lokalt. I den forbindelse samarbejder vi med stærke og toneangivende foreninger om deres specifikke udfordringer og potentialer. 
En del af de foreninger er gymnastikforeninger, hvorfor du får en central rolle i disse udviklingsprocesser. 

Du bliver en del af et fagligt fællesskab i DGI Storkøbenhavns idrætsteam og vil også arbejde sammen med administrative medarbejdere og foreningskonsulenter.  

Din profil:

• Faglig viden om gymnastik og ambitioner for udvikling af idrætten
• Et skarpt blik for både udvikling og udbredelse af kurser og uddannelser
• Erfaring som konsulent eller projektleder – du ved, hvordan man skaber fremdrift og resultater
• Erfaring med foreningsudvikling og gerne kendskab til gymnastikforeningerne i Storkøbenhavn
• En udadvendt og opsøgende tilgang – du trives med at skabe relationer og netværk
• Kompetent bruger af administrative systemer
Praktiske oplysninger

Stillingen er på 37 timer ugentligt. Tiltrædelse 1. februar 2027. 

Det er en tidsbegrænset stilling med udløb 31. marts 2028.

Aften- og weekendarbejde vil forekomme. 

 

DGI Storkøbenhavn

Som idrætsforeningernes udviklingshus styrker vi idrætsforeningerne i en by i konstant forandring. Vi dækker 11 kommuner og repræsenterer ca. 650 idrætsforeninger, der samlet set har mere end 300.000 medlemmer. Vi oplever vækst i medlemstal og samarbejder tæt med foreninger og kommuner om de lokale udviklingsmuligheder.

Vi tilbyder et godt socialt arbejdsmiljø med ca. 55 passionerede medarbejdere og mange frivillige. Kontoret ligger i moderne lokaler centralt i København på Vesterbrogade lige overfor Hovedbanegården.

 

Ansøgning

Ansøgningsfrist er onsdag den 2. december.

Vi holder samtaler mandag den 7. december og anden samtaler torsdag den 10. december.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in AI-driven knowledge graphs and network models of plant stress responses
jobs.description:
The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN) invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in computational plant biology. The project is financed by the Novo Nordisk Foundation through the Ascending Investigator grant “Accelerating crop resilience with AI-enabled gene function prediction and stress regulatory networks” (NNF26OC0113093). The programme aims to make heat and drought resilience engineering in Nordic crops predictable by converting the plant literature and multi-omics data into evidence-backed predictions of gene function and stress regulation.

  Start date is expected to be 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project  Most plant genes remain functionally uncharacterised, and the knowledge that does exist is scattered across more than 200,000 articles. Our knowledge graph PlantConnectome has shown that large language models can extract this knowledge at scale; this project will build its successor and use it to predict gene function.

  You will:

   	
• Fine-tune open large language models (e.g. Llama-class models with QLoRA) on our existing, curated knowledge graph, and use the best checkpoint to extract entities, relationships and supporting evidence from >200,000 open-access plant articles spanning model species and crops 	
• Build a provenance-aware knowledge graph an order of magnitude larger than PlantConnectome, in which every edge is traceable to the sentence and experiment that supports it 	
• Predict new gene–GO associations by direct-neighbourhood reasoning (matching LLM-generated entity definitions to GO terms with embeddings and an LLM guardrail) and by path-based link prediction with graph neural networks, evaluated CAFA-style against held-out annotations 	
• Turn regulatory relationships in the graph into Boolean and related discrete network models of stress signalling, simulate them, and test their predictions against expression data generated in the group 	
• Distinguish well-supported from over-cited claims, and represent evidence quality and independence explicitly in the graph   The position is computational, but sits in a group that generates its own single-cell stress data and validates predictions in rapeseed, so your predictions will be tested.

  Who are we looking for?  We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, physics, mathematics or plant biology with a strong quantitative interest. Experience with natural language processing, large language models, graph databases, network modelling or machine learning is an advantage. An interest in how plants actually work is essential; a formal background in plant biology is not.

  What we value  Coding experience is welcome but not required at entry – we teach it. What we cannot teach quickly, and therefore select for, is scientific judgment:

   	
• questioning data rather than accepting it – asking what was measured, how, and against which expectation 	
• noticing anomalies and treating them as information rather than noise 	
• organising several lines of investigation in parallel and knowing when to stop or redirect one 	
• connecting computational evidence to a concrete biological question 	
• changing your mind when the evidence changes   We are equally interested in candidates from biology who want to learn computation and candidates from computer science, physics or engineering who want to learn biology.

  Our group and research – and what do we offer?  The Mutwil group at PLEN works at the interface of comparative and evolutionary plant biology and AI-driven biological discovery. We build large cross-species gene expression atlases, comparative co-expression networks and knowledge graphs, and we use machine learning and large language models to turn the plant literature and omics archives into testable hypotheses. The group comprises several PhD students, postdocs and master’s students, and maintains a portfolio of widely used community resources under the .plant.tools domain, including PlantConnectome, CoNekt, diurnal.plant.tools and evorepro.plant.tools.

  The group is part of the Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN), Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. We are located on the Frederiksberg Campus in Copenhagen.

  We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern molecular biology laboratories, plant growth facilities and dedicated high-performance computing and GPU resources.

  Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Marek Mutwil, Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN), University of Copenhagen. E-mail: mutwil@plen.ku.dk.

  The PhD programme  A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Qualifications needed

  To be eligible, you must have completed a degree programme equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science, physics, mathematics, molecular biology or a related field. For information on the eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and the Assessment database.

  Terms of employment

  Employment as a PhD fellow is full time and for a maximum of 3 years. Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Responsibilities and tasks   	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Programming experience (e.g. Python) is an advantage; strong analytical reasoning is essential 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience, e.g. with NLP, LLMs, knowledge graphs, network modelling or machine learning 	
• Other relevant professional activities 	
• A curious mind-set with a strong interest in turning scientific literature into predictive, testable models 	
• Good written and spoken English   Application and assessment procedure  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page), stating your motivation for applying for this specific PhD project 	
• Written answers to the four questions below (max. 250 words each). You may use AI tools to help draft your answers; please say so if you do. The written answers are a starting point for the interview, where we will explore your reasoning in conversation. 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor and Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorised English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if possible) 	
• Reference letters (if available)   Application questions

   	
• Research interest. Which biological question would you like to work on in this project, and what evidence would you need to answer it? 	
• Reading data. A gene has an expression value of 100 under control conditions, 200 under heat stress, 200 under drought, and 400 under heat and drought combined. What do you conclude, and what would you want to know before concluding it? 	
• Working in parallel. You have two weeks, a set of publicly available expression data, and a literature you do not yet know. How would you organise the two weeks, and what would you deliver at the end of each? 	
• Changing your mind. Describe a case where you believed something about a project or dataset and evidence made you revise it. What was the evidence?   Application deadline: The deadline for applications is 31 January 2027, 23:59 GMT +1.

The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in March 2027.

jobs.description:
The Centre for Medical Science and Technology Studies at the Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen, invites applications for a 32 month postdoc in Medical Science and Technology Studies/Medical Anthropology. The position is available from February 15, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The postdoc is available via the Carlsberg Foundation Semper Ardens Accelerate-funded project PATHWAYs of precision: AI-driven predictions in neurocognitive and mental illness | Carlsbergfondet.dk, and will employ ethnographic methods to explore the use of predictive Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare and its implications for contemporary medical practice.

   

  Project description

  We seek a highly motivated postdoc with a strong interest in ethnographic research on the social, ethical, and organizational implications of novel digital and data-intensive medical technologies. Specifically, the postdoc will investigate and theorize how predictive AI-based voice biomarker models for the identification and diagnosis of dementia establish new pathways for patient and personhood, professional practice, and healthcare delivery. The postdoc will conduct participant observation in clinical settings at hospitals, qualitative interviews with healthcare professionals, patients, and biomedical/bioinformatics scientists, as well as document analysis of policy papers and clinical guidelines related to AI in healthcare.

   

  Our group and research
 The postdoc will be based at the Centre for Medical Science and Technology Studies (MeST) at the Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen. MeST is a vibrant, internationally recognized, and highly interdisciplinary research environment with scholars from public health, anthropology, sociology, history, psychology, medicine, and philosophy. United by a shared interest in how medical technologies shape and interact with humans and healthcare systems, MeST researchers explore a wide range of topics, with a particular—though not exclusive—focus on precision medicine and digital health. The center provides a stimulating intellectual setting, offering opportunities for collaboration, academic exchange, and methodological innovation.

   

  Principal Investigator is Associate Professor Iben Mundbjerg Gjødsbøl, e-mail: ibgj@sund.ku.dk, direct phone: 35337318.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in generative protein and peptide design for sustainable biomaterials - BRIGHT
jobs.description:
This PhD project is part of a BRIGHT programme developing a general platform for the design of protein- and peptide-based biomaterials, with solid-state battery components as its first testbed. Our goal is to replace fluorinated PFAS polymers with de novo designed proteins and peptides.

You will generate the computational designs at the heart of the platform, by combining molecular foundation models with iterative laboratory feedback. You will develop design algorithms for biomaterials with natural and non-natural amino acids, and for planning their biosynthesis and biomanufacturing. You will develop lab-in-the-loop algorithms that use generative model-controlled stochastic synthesis to maximize information gain at every round of experimental testing.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Responsibilities:

• Generate de novo peptide and protein designs meeting multiple coupled property targets, including adhesion, cohesion, ion conduction and controlled degradability
• Use and adapt generative molecular design tools such as RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN and AlphaFold-type models
• Develop and extend information-dense synthesis algorithms to manufacture designs in the laboratory 
• Extend these methods to expanded genetic codes, so that non-canonical residues can be encoded and biosynthesised rather than only chemically synthesised
• Develop methods to learn from diverse measurements of material properties, via shared latent representations 
• Develop methods to continuously learn from iterative experimentation, by feeding back experimental data into an integrated model with quantified uncertainty
• Work closely with experimentalists to optimize experimental designs for collecting high-information training data
• Work closely with experimentalists to automate and scale up design-build-test-learn cycles
• Report your research results in peer-reviewed scientific publications and international conferences
• Collaborate within the research group and our local, national and international networks
• Disseminate your results through public engagement and social media
• Teach and supervise MSc and BSc students as well as research assistants
Qualifications:

• MSc in computational biology, bioinformatics, biophysics, computer science or a related area
• Programming experience in Python
• Experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch
• Excellent English proficiency in written and oral form
• Excellent communication and social skills for working within an interdisciplinary research team
• Strong analytical skills and ability to work independently
Preferred qualifications but not mandatory:

• Knowledge of protein structure and molecular biology
• Experience with protein design tools such as RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN or AlphaFold
• Familiarity with DNA-encoded libraries, genetic code expansion or next-generation sequencing
• Interest in multi-objective optimisation, reinforcement learning, and bridging computational design with experimental realisation
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. Title:
Maximizing use of fresh grass for dairy cows by combining grazing, zero-grazing, and multispecies swards

Research area and project description:
We are seeking a dedicated PhD student for a 3-year position within the topic of dairy production with fresh grass as a main forage source.

The impact of dairy production on environment and climate is of continued importance and interest. Cropping and feeding fresh grass can potentially improve the impact of dairy production on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen leakage to surrounding fresh waters.

The project investigates the potential of maximizing fresh grass forage intake to reduce enteric methane emission and increase nitrogen utilization, while maintaining milk production. A series of trials with lactating dairy cows are planned investigating combinations of grazing, zero-grazing, and multispecies swards.

jobs.occupation: PhD Fellowship in DNA Replication and Genome Stability After Whole-Genome Doubling
jobs.description:
At the laboratory of Associate Professor Kumar Somyajit, we invite applications for a fully funded PhD fellowship investigating how cells adapt the DNA replication machinery when their genome doubles. The project connects a fundamental challenge in development with a common route of cancer evolution. Previous work in the field of cell cycle and genome integrity and experience in working on embryonic/adult stem cells and cancer cell lines are a plus.

The Somyajit lab, based at the Quantitative Cell Biology and Bioimaging research unit at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, SDU, has a deep interest in studying regulatory foundations of the cell cycle, DNA replication, and genome surveillance in pathophysiology.
Starting date: 01-01-2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. Duration: 3 years as a PhD Student. Interviews of shortlisted candidates will be held in the second week of December 2026. 

Research Project and Role
Whole-genome doubling (WGD) gives a cell an extra copy of its entire genome. It can support specialized functions during development, but it is also common in aggressive cancers, where it can promote chromosome instability and treatment resistance. After WGD, cells must copy and maintain twice as much DNA. The replication and chromatin-maintenance machinery may not increase at the same rate, creating a potential capacity bottleneck.
Our recent work identified PAF15 as a dosage-sensitive regulator of PCNA, the sliding clamp that coordinates DNA replication and repair. PAF15 helps retain PCNA on chromatin and supports maturation of the newly copied lagging strand. Its abundance must stay within a narrow range: too little weakens replication, while excess can disrupt PCNA function (PMID: 41606318; Nature. 2026 Mar;651(8105):521-532. doi: 10.1038/s41586-025-10011-3). 
Building on this work, the PhD project will investigate whether whole-genome doubling creates capacity limits in the machinery that copies and maintains the genome in non-transformed cells, cancer cells and mouse embryonic stem cells, how cells adapt to these limits, and whether the resulting dependencies could provide opportunities to target cancer cells.

The project combines quantitative cell biology, genome engineering and biochemical approaches. Methods will include quantitative image-based cytometry (QIBC), live-cell imaging, super-resolution microscopy, DNA fibre assays, CRISPR-based perturbation, stem-cell culture and differentiation, and chromatin-resolved mass spectrometry.
You will work closely with researchers in the Somyajit group and collaborators at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology. SDU provides an international and interdisciplinary research environment with advanced facilities for bioimaging, cell biology, sequencing, flow cytometry, mass spectrometry and metabolomics.

The Somyajit group is located at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, SDU. The department constitutes an international, ambitious, highly dynamic, and well-equipped working environment with state-of-the-art facilities for advanced bioimaging, quantitative mechanistic cell biology, next generation sequencing, single-cell transcriptomics, flow cytometry, mass spectrometry, metabolomics, and transgenic mouse work. Strategic research alliances exist with Odense University Hospital (OUH).

Qualifications/requirements
We are looking for highly motivated, dedicated, and ambitious candidates with:

• 
A master’s degree in Life Science, preferable Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Biomedicine (the 5+3 program). 

• 
Curious mind-set with a strong interest in fundamental Cell cycle, DNA replication and Genome integrity.

• 
Relevant laboratory experience in quantitative imaging and genome editing.

• 
Know-how in Genome integrity field, stem cell culture, light microscopy, bioinformatics will be considered an advantage.

• 
Strong communication and collaborative skills and an interest in working in an interdisciplinary environment.

• 
Proficiency in spoken and written English.

Requirements and programme structure
PhD candidates follow an individual PhD plan including course work, conference participation, and teaching. One semester is typically spent at another research institution - often abroad. The scholarship carries a monthly salary including pension plus office facilities and financial support for conference travels and research visits abroad.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in Leptin Gene Regulation and Adipocyte Biology
jobs.description:
The Mandrup group invites applications from outstanding candidates for a Postdoctoral position in our group based at the Functional Genomics & Metabolism Research Unit, Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, University of Southern Denmark. The position is offered for a duration of up to three years and will be available from January 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Project and Research Environment
The Postdoctoral Fellow will work on a project focusing on the molecular mechanisms regulating human leptin (LEP) gene expression in adipocytes. The aim is to identify the cis-regulatory elements, transcription factors, and signaling pathways controlling LEP expression during adipocyte differentiation and in mature adipocytes, and to understand how chromatin architecture and physiological signals are integrated to regulate leptin production. To address these questions, the project combines complementary, state-of-the-art approaches, including:

• 
Chromatin conformation analyses (e.g., Region-Capture Micro-C, Capture-C, and related approaches)

• 
Epigenomic profiling (e.g., ATAC-seq, CUT&Tag, and DynaTag)

• 
Genome editing and perturbation approaches (e.g., CRISPRi, CRISPR/Cas9, and siRNA-mediated knockdown)

• 
Transcriptomic and multi-omics analyses

• 
Computational modelling of gene regulatory networks and integration with clinical and physiological data

The project is embedded in an interdisciplinary research environment that combines molecular biology, functional genomics, computational biology, and translational studies in primary human adipocytes.

Job Description
The Postdoctoral fellow will drive experimental activities and contribute to the scientific development of the project. The position requires both independent work and close collaboration within the research group.
Key responsibilities include:

• 
Designing and conducting experiments investigating the regulation of human leptin (LEP) gene expression

• 
Generating and analyzing transcriptomic, epigenomic, and chromatin conformation datasets

• 
Integrating multi-omics, physiological, and clinical data to identify regulatory networks governing leptin expression

• 
Implementing and optimizing advanced molecular, genomic, and computational methods in adipocyte model systems and primary human adipocytes

In addition, the candidate will:

• 
Contribute to supervision and mentoring of students

• 
Participate in preparation of scientific publications and dissemination of results

• 
Actively contribute to a collaborative, ambitious, and supportive research environment

Qualifications
We are seeking a highly motivated candidate with a strong postdoctoral research profile and expertise in functional genomics and the molecular regulation of gene expression.
Required qualifications:

• 
A PhD in molecular biology, genomics, biochemistry, or a related field

• 
Strong background and experimental skills in molecular biology, functional genomics, and transcriptional regulation

• 
Ability to independently drive research projects

• 
Strong collaborative and communication skills

• 
Proficiency in spoken and written English

In addition, the following qualifications are relevant but not required: 

• 
Hands-on experience with adipocyte biology, metabolic research, or cellular differentiation systems

• 
Experience with chromatin conformation methods (e.g., Capture-C, Micro-C, Hi-C, or related approaches)

• 
Experience with epigenomic and transcriptomic techniques (e.g., ATAC-seq, CUT&Tag, RNA-seq, or related sequencing-based assays)

• 
Experience with analysis and integration of multi-omics datasets

• 
Experience with computational biology, bioinformatics pipelines, and R for data analysis and visualization

• 
Hands-on experience with genome editing and gene perturbation technologies (e.g., CRISPR/Cas9, CRISPRi, or RNA interference)

We offer

• 
A position in a focused, externally funded research project at the forefront of chromatin biology research

• 
Access to state-of-the-art infrastructure within genomics, imaging, and molecular biology

• 
An international, highly collaborative, and dynamic research environment

• 
Strong support for scientific development and career progression

• 
Competitive salary and comprehensive social benefits

The Mandrup Group
The Mandrup Group has a long-standing interest in the detailed molecular mechanisms governing transcriptional control of adipocyte differentiation. We apply a variety of sequencing-based, computational, and molecular technologies, combined with loss- and gain-of-function strategies to study the mechanisms and role of the 3D chromatin architecture, the crosstalk between enhancers in enhancer communities and the role of specific transcription factors.
You will work closely together with other postdoctoral fellows and PhD students in the group, and you will also be expected to collaborate with colleagues in the Center of Excellence in Functional Genomics and Tissue Plasticity (ATLAS) and Center of Adipocyte Signaling (ADIPOSIGN), both directed by Susanne Mandrup. Furthermore, you will be able to benefit from the many international collaborations of our group.

The Functional Genomics & Metabolism Research Unit 
The Mandrup Group is located in the Functional Genomics & Metabolism Research Unit at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, SDU. The research unit currently hosts eight independent research groups focusing on how specific cell types regulate gene expression and how this affects the development and function of cells and tissues. Thus, our research aims to better understand how genes regulate human physiology and diseases such as obesity, fatty liver disease, cancer, and diabetes. The research unit constitutes an international, ambitious, highly dynamic, and well-equipped working environment. The unit and the department have state-of-the-art facilities for next-generation sequencing, single-cell transcriptomics and epigenomics, flow cytometry, mass spectrometry, metabolomics, bioimaging, cell culture, and dietary intervention and transgenic mouse models. The unit maintains strategic research alliances with Odense University Hospital (OUH). This provides a highly stimulating research environment with numerous opportunities for learning and developing new ideas.
